transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this planning roundtable for the proposed six-week peer-tutoring program for our middle school students in grades 6 through 8. Before I can sign off on the approval, I need to gather input from each of you on the relevant aspects of the draft plan. As you know, the current plan calls for two adult supervisors, Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and paper consent forms collected before the program begins. I'd like to go around the table and hear from each of you -- the teacher, counselor, technology coordinator, and family liaison -- about any concerns, requirements, or recommendations you have related to your area of expertise. Let's start with the teacher. What are your thoughts on the proposed plan?

transcript.text: I need to flag an important staffing issue. Yesterday I received the finalized roster from the activities office, and it contains 18 student tutors. However, the draft plan still lists the preliminary staffing estimate of two adult supervisors. Our school's supervision rule permits one adult to supervise no more than six tutors in an active tutoring session, which means 18 tutors would require at least three adult supervisors, not two.

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical concern about the student-selected tutor pairings. My student-support review this week found two active no-contact restrictions involving prospective tutors and students seeking tutoring. These restrictions are recorded only in confidential counseling files, so no one else at this table would be aware of them. Because of these restrictions, tutor pairings cannot be student-selected -- they must be assigned and monitored by me as counselor to ensure we don't violate those no-contact orders.

transcript.text: I need to raise an important concern about the consent form process. I confirmed the procedure with the family-engagement office this week, and for this program, family consent must be entered into the student information system before a student can participate. Additionally, the district has approved translated electronic forms in addition to paper forms. However, the draft plan still describes only paper consent form collection without any SIS entry requirement. This needs to be updated to require that consent be recorded in the SIS, and the electronic translated forms should be made available to ensure all families can participate.
